text: This is Gene Larson, News Director of Radio Station KGSW in Karniakoska.
Right at the present time, on this Tuesday evening, November the 5th, 1957,
we are in our studio, the time is Central Standard Time, 720.
At our side, at microphone, we have Mr. Reinhold O. Schmidt.
That's Reinhold O. Schmidt, S-C-H-M-I-D-T.
Mr. Schmidt has stated that his home address is Melling and Bakersfield, California,
at 715 Gates Street, and that he is employed by Value Pack Incorporated.
They're in the wholesale K-Feed and Grain Concentrate.
Their office is at 501 West Main Street at Brawley, California.
That's B-R-A-W-L-E-Y.
Mr. Schmidt, this afternoon I believe you had something occur to you,
and you talked a little bit about it.
of questions. The information that I have given so far, Mr. Schmidt, is that correct?
Yes.
In other words, you work for Value Pack Incorporated. You live in Bakersfield. You are in Kearney,
Nebraska for what, sir?
Buying grain.
And is this your first trip to Kearney?
Yes.
And by buying grain, what do you mean, sir?
Buying from the farmers or elevators.
And you travel around the country, is that it, sir?
Yes.
And you drive what kind of a car, sir?
A Seaworth.
What's your...
55 Super.
Now this afternoon I believe you were out south of town, south of Kearney.
About how far, sir?
I would say about four miles.
About what time was this, sir?
Between two and three in the afternoon.
And you were headed in which direction, sir?
I was going south and then turning east on the Newark Highway.
And you were up the cement road on this Newark Road for about how long a time?
I mean mileage-wise.
Oh, it was about a mile.
About a mile.
and then noticed something in the Platte River bed.
Am I right that it's dry?
There was a flash there when I first noticed the flash.
And that was how far from the road, sir?
About, I would say, a half a mile.
A half a mile from the road at the present time.
Did you continue to drive, or did you immediately stop?
No, I drove on up a little closer to where the flash was
to see what caused that.
When I got too close, I found out.

crash there. You thought it was a balloon that had crashed? Yes. And then you drove closer to the object? Yes. And then what occurred? I got within 60 feet of the object. My car stopped. The motor went dead. The motor went dead. I tried to step out of it, but there was no response whatsoever. Then what did you do, Mr. Smith? I got out of the car. I figured maybe the terminal had just broken loose in the car. I got out of the car and walked toward this balloon, what I thought was this balloon. And when I got within 30 feet of it,
light shot out and i would say it paralyzed me either paralyzed there or else if the
hippopotamus on the way you couldn't move physically could you think yes i could take
it off and i couldn't move i see uh before we go into further happenstance with this object
uh i wonder if you could describe it for me about how long was it sir it was about 100 feet long as
We get to step off there.
It's about 100 feet long and 30 feet wide, and now it's 14 feet high.
What did it appear to be made out of?
A real bright aluminum.
Now, this was in the riverbed of the Platte River, which is dry at the present time.
Yeah, it's sandy there.
Yes.
And it appeared to be of aluminum.
It was bright and shiny.
And you got out and you approached this object.
Yeah.
And you described it.
Did you notice anything as to how it would be moved?
Did there appear to be pipes or propellers or what was it, sir?
On each end of the machine, there was a tube running up and down,
and in these tubes, as I can see, were big fans.
And one seemed like that's done the propellant.
How close did you get to this object?
I got to it and in it.
I understand that, sir.
But before you got into it, you got out of your car, went across the field toward the riverbed.
said, how far did you get toward the object before you noticed anybody?
Oh, about 30 feet.
About 30 feet.
And then what occurred?
That's when that light shot out and paralyzed as far as you know.
Then what occurred, sir?
There was two men came up, and they said not to be alarmed if they would have to search me.
How did they come out of the side?
Yes, out of the side of the machine.
And were there steps down to the ground, or did they jump?
There was a sliding door, and then the step.
I see. And they came out and they spoke to you in English?
Yes.
How were they dressed?
They were dressed like any American would be.
In business suits?
In business suits, yes.
I see. Did they appear to be young or middle-aged?
They were middle-aged. I would say between 40 and 40.
And they spoke good English?
Yes.
No, they spoke broken English.
Broken English.
What did they say to you?
They told me not to feel alarmed.
They were not going to hurt me.
and they did want to search me.
And I told them I had no weapons.
And I asked them what the deal was or what the object was.
And they said, well, as long as we can leave for a few minutes,
you can just walk in and look around.
So you went up the steps with them?
Yes.
You entered the object?
Into the object.
Did you sense anything by way of smell,
sight that was out of the ordinary?
Not at all.
Not at all.
Were there any other people in this object?
Yes, there was four men and two ladies.
What age did they appear to be?
They appeared to be around 40.
Were they talking when you entered?
They just spoke to me, that's all.
What did they say?
They just said hello.
In what? In what language?
In American language.
In American language.
They said hello, and you answered them?
Yes.
I see.
And what did you felt once you got inside of this object?
Well, there was just a lot of instruments and wires,
and it seemed like they were working on these walkways for some reason,
and the girls were at another instrument there with a lot of dials and pushpulls.
After they said hello to you, these women and these other men, or were there no other men?
There were two men and three women?
There were four men and two women.
All right, then one of them more than likely sort of stayed by you, one man all the time, by you.
Yes.
And he was the one that talked to you, perhaps?
Yes.
other two women and other three men went about their business?
Yes.
Did they appear to be interested in you?
No.
Did they talk among themselves?
Yes.
And what language did they talk?
They were talking in a high German, as much as whatever I could.
The professor's machine was about 100 feet long as I stated,
and they were talking in a high German every time I could hear them.
Are you qualified to know high German, Mr. Schmidt?
Yes.
You've had schooling in it, or your parents each in one way or another?
I see.
And they didn't appear to be interested in you personally?
No.
After they said hello.
Now, you were in for the object about how long, Mr. Schmuck?
I was in an object there, I would say, about 30 minutes.
30 minutes.
What did you do while you were in there?
I was just talking to this man, although he didn't explain anything to me.
Did you ask him questions?
Yes.
I asked him more about what they were doing.
He said, well, he couldn't tell me that, but in the near future, we might all know, he said.
in the nearest district.
To tell my people that they meant no harm.
They meant no harm.
Yes.
That's the statement he made.
Yes.
And you were in there for approximately 30 minutes.
And then did something occur that would indicate to you
that perhaps the machinery was repaired?
Yes.
They said that this one man was working at one end.
He said they would be ready to take off.
In the German language.
In the German.
And you recognized it.
Yes, I recognized it.
It's still high German.
Yes.
And then this man told me in American
They would register and take off, and I would have to leave.
I went out of this machine, and the water roller went up.
I stepped back, I would say, about 10 feet.
They didn't tell me to not watch them or anything.
I stepped back about 10 feet, and then once the machine started going,
I probably stepped back a little farther, and then I watched them leave.
How did they leave?
It went straight up in the air.
Straight up in the air?
Yeah, slowly.
Slowly, slowly, at first, and it gained speed until it got...
About 150 or 200 feet up in the air.
It seemed like there was a flash there, and it just disappeared.
Now, you can see any object of this size 150 feet in the air.
Oh, yeah.
But this one disappeared.
Just disappeared.
They changed color.
Did they have any instructions to you after you left?
Did they tell you not to do something or do something?
I mean, what were they, did they say anything to you after, with regards to starting your automobile, let's say?
Oh, they told me not to, when I left, they said don't try and start your automobile.
They have to leave so it won't start anyway.
I see.
And kind of smiled.
That's for sure that they had done something to the automobile.
Did you personally feel that they were friendly towards you?
Yes, very friendly.
Very friendly.
Very, very friendly.
But disinterested in you as a person?
Yes.
I see.
Let me ask you this now, Mr. Schmidt.
You were with them or near their object and with them for about how long a time, sir?
I would say about 30, the sheriff.
Let me ask you this.
Why were you scared?
Not that I was so much until I've seen something.
Yes, yes, yes.
I think I probably should say, I believe that was a crash, sir.
You came in and talked to the Buffalo County Sheriff, Lloyd Frank.
Was that right?
Yes.
And then what occurred?
And me and the sheriff and myself, we went out there.
And something had been there.
We've come back and got the city manager.
That's Ray Lundy.
Yes.
And the chief of police.
Chief of police.
That's Besson Nelson.
That's right.
And how have you returned to the team now?
Was there any evidence left at the scene that would indicate that this happened?
Yes, the sheriff, I think it was,
when I thought we picked up some leaves that had some,
what we thought was oil or hydraulic oil, we don't know.
It had a sugar smell to it.
Did you identify the smell?
No.
A very peculiar smell.
It was a greenish color.
Were there marks in the ground?
It seemed like this one, we could see where this one hydraulic shift had hit the ground.
I see. Were there footprints where these men had walked?
Well, it was sandy, yes, there was footprints there.
And you explained to them what had happened, and they were convinced that some of this had occurred, if not all.
Oh, good.
Absolutely.
What are your personal feelings, Mr. Schmidt, about this?
Have you had a chance to calm down enough to actually give up?
I really haven't so far, but I have...
The thing is that how the space or machines from our space
could be from different countries.
You feel it might be one of the two?
Yes.
You didn't notice anything foreign about them
other than they might have been just...
Yes.
Would you say...
What race would you say they were?
German. You will obey German.
Well, Mr. Schmidt, we want to thank you very much for the opportunity of talking with you.
We appreciate it very much.
You're going to be very definitely interrogated by the various law enforcement bodies,
and there will be other news medias after you.
We appreciate the chance to talk to you firsthand about this.
Do you have anything else that you'd like to say at this time?
No, I guess that's all that I have.
All right, thank you very, very much.
Mr. Reinhold O. Schmidt of Bakersfield, California.
This is Gene Larson, news director for KGFW in Tarny, Nebraska.
